110
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, September 5, 2012/Bhadra 14, 1934 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Commerce and Industry; Culture; Defence; Home Affairs;
Housing and Urban Poverty  Alleviation; Labour and Employment;
Textiles; Urban Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Treatment of needy people under
RSBY in Uttarakhand
†*341. SHRI BHAGAT SINGH
KOSHYARI: Will the Minister of
LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether financial assistance is
provided to the people for their treatment
through the smart card issued under the
Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY);
(b) if so, the State-wise number of such
needy people, including Uttarakhand, and
names of the districts of Uttarakhand where
these cards have been issued;
(c) since when the scheme is being
implemented and the number of persons
included under this scheme and the number
of people proposed to be included
thereunder; and
(d) whether the scheme is running far
behind the target?
Non-extension of loan waiver scheme
to small powerlooms
*342. SHRI DEVENDER GOUD T.:
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased
to state:
(a) the progress of the loan waiver
scheme of the Ministry, with particular
reference to Andhra Pradesh;
(b) whether it is a fact that the
Ministry's loan waiver scheme has not been
extended to small powerloom weavers
present in the villages; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
Development plan for cities and
towns
*343. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has chalked
out any development plan to bring
improvement in urbanization in the selected
cities and towns of the country;
(b) if so, the city and town-wise details
thereof, especially in Andhra Pradesh; and
(c) the number of cities in which houses
are proposed to be built and by when they
are likely to be completed?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

111
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Hindu families migrated from
Pakistan
†*344. SHRIMA TI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of Hindu families from Baluchistan and
Sindh provinces of Pakistan are reaching
India at Attari Border;
(b) if so, the details of Hindu families
who migrated from Pakistan to India during
the past three years, along with the
atrocities meted out to them in Pakistan;
(c) the details of the permission sought
by Hindus migrated from Pakistan
regarding their stay in India; and
(d) the details of the incidents of
occupying the houses and lands of Hindus
in Pakistan and demolition of Temples
and Gurudwaras during the past three
years?
Introduction of Indian systems of
medicine in armed forces
*345. DR. CHANDAN MITRA: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Indian systems of medicine
have not been introduced in the armed forces
in the country;
(b) if so, the detailed scientific reasons
therefor; and
(c) the immediate steps taken by
Government for re-imbursement of
expenses on Ayurvedic treatment of the
Army personnel who opt for Indian
systems of medicine?
Investment made by Wal-Mart/Cedar
in form of CCD
*346. SHRI M.P. ACHUTHAN: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Wal-Mart
has made Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)
in the form of Compulsory Convertible
Debentures (CCD) amounting to
` 455.80 crores in March, 2010 in a
company called Cedar Support Services
Limited;
(b) if so, whether this investment was
made under the automatic route or with
FIPB approval;
(c) whether the Wal-Mart/Cedar has
made any declaration regarding the end use
of the FDI funds at the time of investment
by Wal-Mart; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Contract workers in automobile
industry
*347. SHRI A. ELAV ARASAN: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether nearly 40 per cent of the
workers employed by automobile industry
are contract workers;
(b) whether it is a fact that car makers
use cheap contract workers in key
functions whereas they are supposed to be
employed only in non-critical areas and
thus are exploited by the automobile
industry extensively;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether these workers are fired
without notice as they have no legal
protection; if so, the details thereof; and

112
(e) the steps taken by Government to
investigate the pathetic condition of the
contract workers?
Unutilised funds lying in
Construction Workers
Welfare Boards
*348. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than
` 7000 crore are lying unutilised in different
State Construction Workers Welfare Boards
but this amount could not be spent due to
inaction of the State Government Labour
Departments; and
(b) if so, the details of funds available in
different States in Construction Worke
